source_metadata.title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_metadata.original_or_revised_title_if_discussed: Originally The Psychology of Everyday Things; retitled The Design of Everyday Things; this uploaded source is the revised and expanded edition.
source_metadata.author: Don Norman
source_metadata.publisher: Basic Books, a member of the Perseus Books Group
source_metadata.original_publication_history_visible: Original edition title and retitling discussed in front/back matter of uploaded source.
source_metadata.source_format: Uploaded ZIP containing an EPUB 2 package with OPF, NCX, XHTML/HTML, CSS, and JPEG figures.

non_negotiable_distinctions: knowledge in head vs knowledge in world
gulf of execution vs gulf of evaluation
capture slip vs description-similarity slip vs mode error
warning vs constraint vs forcing function
canonical_review_gate: What goal are they trying to accomplish?
What signifiers indicate where or how to act?
What does the user believe will happen?
How well does action map to effect?
What knowledge exists in the world?
What invalid or dangerous actions are allowed?
Is the observed failure a slip or a mistake?
Can the user recover without expert help?
What observed user evidence supports the diagnosis?
diagnostic_protocol: name observed behavior and evidence quality
inspect only relevant mechanisms, not the whole stack every time
avoid user blame before system diagnosis
separate source-supported principle from applied extension
do_not_do: do not say intuitive without observation
do not assume training is the answer
do not treat aesthetics as usability evidence
do not claim accessibility/platform compliance without current verification
do not paste the canonical review gate into every record

active_record_groups.core_concepts: Core concepts and canonical review gate.
active_record_groups.mapping_feedback_constraints: Mapping, feedback, constraints, and forcing functions.
active_record_groups.knowledge: Knowledge in head/world and memory-burden records.
active_record_groups.prevention_recovery: Reusable risk, prevention, and recovery records.

core_concepts.name: Canonical HCD review gate
core_concepts.summary: A single reusable gate for broad human-centered design review; individual records reference this rather than repeating it.

core_concepts.name: Discoverability of possible action and state
core_concepts.summary: People need enough perceivable information to know what can be done and what state exists.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when the user cannot identify available action or current state before acting.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether action/state cues need to be made perceivable at the point of need.

core_concepts.name: Understanding of operation and result
core_concepts.summary: A user may find an action but still misunderstand what it does or what the result means.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when action is visible but prediction or interpretation is wrong.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether the system image needs clearer explanation, naming, or feedback content.

core_concepts.name: Seven stages of action as diagnostic sequence
core_concepts.summary: A task can fail at goal formation, intention, action specification, execution, perception, interpretation, or evaluation.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use to locate where a workflow breaks rather than labeling the whole experience as confusing.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Which stage needs design support: action choice, execution, feedback, interpretation, or evaluation.

core_concepts.name: Human-centered design starts with observed people and real tasks
core_concepts.summary: Design reasoning must begin from people’s goals, context, abilities, and observed behavior, not from the implementation alone.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when a design recommendation lacks user/task evidence.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to observe, prototype, test, or reframe before prescribing a fix.

core_concepts.name: Investigate the design before blaming the person
core_concepts.summary: Repeated human difficulty is evidence to inspect the system, task, feedback, constraints, and social setting.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when errors are being explained as carelessness, resistance, or lack of intelligence.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to redesign cues, constraints, state, and recovery before prescribing training.

core_concepts.name: Training may compensate for missing system cues
core_concepts.summary: When repeated routine tasks need repeated explanations, the design may be moving knowledge into heads that belongs in the world.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when support, cheat sheets, or onboarding cover the same routine gap repeatedly.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to externalize the explanation into labels, examples, constraints, defaults, or visible state.

core_concepts.name: Design for error prevention and recovery
core_concepts.summary: Design should prevent predictable errors where possible and make recovery clear when errors occur.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when a system allows invalid states or makes repair expert-dependent.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to add constraints, reversible actions, clearer error states, or targeted retry paths.

core_concepts.name: Observed user behavior outranks abstract principle selection
core_concepts.summary: The reasoning OS should guide investigation, but current observations, tests, screenshots, logs, and user feedback determine diagnosis.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when an assistant is tempted to assert a diagnosis without behavioral evidence.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to recommend evidence collection before redesign.

core_concepts.name: Separate conceptual confidence from empirical diagnosis confidence
core_concepts.summary: A Norman concept may be strongly supported while a claim about a specific user behavior remains uncertain until observed.
core_concepts.distinct_diagnostic_value: Use when a design principle is clear but the available evidence is weak.
core_concepts.specific_design_decision: Whether to label the recommendation as a hypothesis, direct principle, or verified diagnosis.

terminology_index.important_distinction: An affordance is not the mark, label, or cue that advertises the action.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Check whether the action is actually possible, not merely labeled.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not call every visual cue an affordance.

terminology_index.important_distinction: A signifier communicates; it does not by itself create the action possibility.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Check labels, placement, shape, state, and conventions that tell people what to do.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not treat signifiers as decorative labels.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Visibility may expose elements; discoverability requires usable meaning for action.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Observe whether people can identify the next valid action without instructions.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not equate a visible button with a discoverable action.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Visibility is a contributor to discoverability, not the whole diagnostic category.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Inspect whether important state and available actions can be seen at the time of need.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not make everything visible when progressive disclosure would reduce burden.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Discoverability is about finding possible action; understanding is about interpreting operation and outcome.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Ask users to predict what an action will do and explain what happened afterward.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not assume that finding a button means understanding the system.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Confirmation asks permission or acknowledgement; feedback reports action/result/state.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Specify timing, content, target, and next step for the feedback.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not use a generic spinner when the user needs status or result details.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Confirmation is not a substitute for showing actual result after action.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use it selectively where reversibility is low or intent is ambiguous.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not add confirmation dialogs to every action.

terminology_index.important_distinction: A label can name an action; mapping lets users predict which action produces which effect.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Test whether people can predict an effect from control position, order, and naming.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not solve a mapping problem with only longer instructions.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Natural mapping is about correspondence, not just consistent vocabulary.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Arrange controls so the structure suggests the effect.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not call arbitrary order natural because it is familiar to the designer.

terminology_index.important_distinction: A constraint changes what can happen; a warning merely asks the user to comply.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Identify invalid states the design can make impossible.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not rely on warnings when the system can prevent the error.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Physical constraints work through fit and possibility rather than meaning.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use shape or compatibility to prevent wrong assembly or wrong selection where possible.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not describe a policy rule as a physical constraint.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Cultural constraints depend on shared conventions and may vary by population.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Validate icon, color, order, and gesture meanings with the target user group.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not assume the designer’s convention is universal.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Semantic constraints use meaning; logical constraints use relations among remaining possibilities.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Ask what actions the task meaning itself rules out.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not use semantic explanations when users lack the domain meaning.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Logical constraints rely on relational structure rather than social convention or task meaning alone.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Show completeness, one-to-one correspondence, and remaining unmatched items.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not hide the set of remaining possibilities.

terminology_index.important_distinction: The designed or communicated conceptual model is not identical to what a user actually believes.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Check whether the interface teaches the right operating idea.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not expose implementation details and call that a conceptual model.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Mental model is the user’s belief; conceptual model may be the designer’s intended explanation.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Elicit user predictions to detect mismatch.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not infer a mental model from one click without evidence.

terminology_index.important_distinction: The interface is part of the system image, but the system image includes behavior, labels, documentation, feedback, and results.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Audit what the system communicates through all user-facing signals.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not assume the designer’s model reaches users unless the system image communicates it.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Head knowledge can be efficient but is fragile under interruption, rarity, and stress.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Identify what people must memorize to complete the task.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not remove every memory demand; learned expertise can be valuable.

terminology_index.important_distinction: World knowledge reduces memorization but can be slower or cluttering if overused.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Move fragile steps, state, and prerequisites into visible cues.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not confuse documentation hidden elsewhere with usable world knowledge.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Execution asks how to do it; evaluation asks what happened.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Diagnose whether the user can choose and perform the next action.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not repair execution failures only with success messages.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Evaluation is about sensemaking after action, not choosing the action.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Check whether outcome, status, meaning, and next step are visible.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not treat completion as clear if the user cannot interpret the result.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Execution gap precedes or occurs during action choice and performance.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Ask what the user wants to do and which action appears to do it.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not misclassify a result-interpretation problem as execution.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Evaluation gap appears when the user cannot tell what happened or what it means.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Observe repeated checking, duplicate action, or requests for status meaning.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not assume feedback solved evaluation if it lacks interpretable content.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Slip diagnosis focuses on execution, attention, habit, memory, and target discrimination.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Ask whether the user knew what they wanted to do before the failure.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not prescribe conceptual training for a simple target-selection slip.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Mistake diagnosis focuses on knowledge, rules, and conceptual model, not motor execution alone.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Ask what rule or understanding led to the action.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not treat every wrong action as a slip.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Capture is sequence/habit dominance; description-similarity is wrong target similarity.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Look for actions that begin correctly and then veer into a more practiced routine.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not blame carelessness when design lets routine overpower intention.

terminology_index.important_distinction: The failure is target discrimination, not habitual sequence takeover.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Increase perceptual and semantic separation between confusable targets.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not solve target similarity only with training.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Mode error depends on hidden or misunderstood state-dependent meanings.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Make mode visible, reduce mode dependence, or make actions mode-independent.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not rely on memory of mode when consequence is high.

terminology_index.important_distinction: A lapse can occur despite a correct plan; it is not necessarily misunderstanding.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Support resumption, checkpoints, and visible sequence state.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not assume the user never learned the task.

terminology_index.important_distinction: The user has a rule, but it is the wrong rule for this situation or is misapplied.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Improve discrimination cues and rule-condition visibility.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not over-explain the whole system when the rule cue is the failure.

terminology_index.important_distinction: The user lacks an adequate rule/model rather than merely choosing the wrong known rule.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Strengthen conceptual model, examples, and interpretable feedback.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not blame lack of attention when the situation is genuinely novel.

terminology_index.important_distinction: A forcing function changes the action path rather than merely cautioning.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use when missing a condition creates serious error or rework.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not overuse forcing functions where they create needless blockage.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Lock-in preserves required continuation; lockout blocks entry or action.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use where premature exit would cause loss or danger.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not trap users without a safe recovery route.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Lockout prevents an action; lock-in prevents premature discontinuation.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use to block actions that should not be available under current conditions.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not hide why an action is locked out.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Interlock enforces sequence; confirmation asks for acknowledgment.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use when ordering matters and wrong order causes harm or unrecoverable failure.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not use an interlock when simple feedback would be enough.

terminology_index.important_distinction: HCD is evidence-driven and iterative, not simply asking people what they like.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Observe real work and test prototypes against actual behavior.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not call a design human-centered because it is aesthetically preferred.

terminology_index.important_distinction: Iteration expects failures to reveal design information.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Use test results and repeated breakdowns to revise the design.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not treat first-release failure as proof users are incompetent.

terminology_index.important_distinction: More automation can reduce practice and increase dependence during abnormal conditions.
terminology_index.observable_design_implication: Design automation with visibility, handoff, monitoring, and recovery support.
terminology_index.misuse_warning: Do not assume automation removes human-error responsibility from design.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Correct intention but wrong action or forgotten step.
human_error_index.execution_state: Execution or memory deviates from intention.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Prevention differs: make correct execution easier and wrong execution harder, rather than teaching a concept the user already knows.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Motor or attention slip selects the wrong action.
human_error_index.execution_state: Physical/action execution goes to wrong control, timing, or target.
observable_behavior_signals: wrong button adjacent to intended one
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Target layout and discrimination matter more than explaining the task.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: The intended action drops out of memory.
human_error_index.execution_state: Step, goal, or planned future action is forgotten.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: The fix is resumption support, not simply telling people to remember.

human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: Less frequent intended sequence starts correctly.
human_error_index.execution_state: Dominant habitual sequence takes over after shared opening.
observable_behavior_signals: begins correct workflow then completes familiar wrong one
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: The uncommon path must be distinguished at the divergence point.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: The user selects a confusable target.
human_error_index.execution_state: Wrong object matches a similar description, look, or location.
observable_behavior_signals: says “I thought this was the other one”
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: The design should increase discrimination between targets.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Action meaning depends on hidden mode.
human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: Intention may be correct for assumed mode.
human_error_index.execution_state: Same action is interpreted under a different actual mode/state.
observable_behavior_signals: performs live action while thinking dry-run
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Mode visibility and mode reduction prevent recurrence better than admonitions.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: The user acts reasonably from a wrong model or rule.
human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: Goal, plan, or interpretation is wrong.
human_error_index.execution_state: Action follows an incorrect understanding or plan.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Mistake prevention strengthens conceptual model and rule cues.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: A familiar rule fits the cues incorrectly.
human_error_index.execution_state: Wrong rule chosen or known rule misapplied.
observable_behavior_signals: applies old procedure to new case
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Clarify the cue that selects the correct rule.
recovery_patterns_specific_to_this_error: explain why rule does not apply

human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: No adequate rule/model exists for the situation.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Strengthen conceptual model and exploratory feedback.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Local pressures make violation seem rational.
human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: User knowingly bypasses rule or procedure.
human_error_index.execution_state: Action is intentional but violates expected process.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Design must address constraints and incentives, not just knowledge.

human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: Goal or plan may be correct before interruption.
human_error_index.execution_state: Resumption lacks state and next-step cues.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Support resumption rather than assuming uninterrupted attention.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Time, authority, incentives, or norms shape error.
human_error_index.execution_state: Organizational context pressures unsafe or brittle behavior.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: The system around the interface may be part of the design problem.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Errors remain hidden from design learning.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Reporting quality affects prevention and resilience.

human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: Error has occurred or is developing.
human_error_index.execution_state: User/system does not notice until later consequence.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Detection needs timely, interpretable state information.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Small failures cascade into abandonment or expert rescue.
human_error_index.execution_state: System cannot absorb, signal, or recover gracefully.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Design should assume errors and support adaptation.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: Automation reduces routine burden but can increase recovery difficulty.
human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: User relies on automation during routine work.
human_error_index.execution_state: Rare abnormal condition requires understanding no longer practiced.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Automation needs system image, monitoring, and recovery support.

human_error_index.distinct_failure_mechanism: The confirmation no longer distinguishes risk.
human_error_index.intention_or_plan_state: User intends to proceed through repeated confirmations.
human_error_index.execution_state: Confirmation becomes a routinized action rather than a meaningful check.
human_error_index.why_the_distinction_matters: Confirmation must be meaningful or replaced with undo/constraints.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: User cannot discover an available action.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Expose or signpost the action at the point of need.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Cue is visible but does not communicate action meaning or distinction.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Clarify user-level meaning and discrimination.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Control/action does not correspond predictably to effect.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Rearrange, rename, or group by action-effect relation.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Action produces no perceivable response.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Acknowledge receipt and state change.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Long operation lacks progress or status.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Show processing phase and safe options.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Mode, selection, filter, readiness, or processing state is invisible.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Persist state near dependent actions.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: The system requires fragile remembered steps, names, paths, or future actions.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Move memory burden into visible world knowledge.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Same action changes effect based on hidden or weakly signified mode.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Make mode visible or reduce mode dependence.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Targets/actions are too similar to distinguish under realistic conditions.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Increase perceptual and semantic discrimination.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Habitual sequence can take over uncommon intended sequence.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Differentiate path at divergence and insert goal checkpoint.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Irreversible or high-consequence action is too easy or poorly distinguished.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Use target clarity, reversibility, and meaningful commitment.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: System lets user proceed into preventable failure.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Constrain, gate, or validate earlier with clear remedy.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: After failure, users cannot understand or repair the state.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Preserve work, identify cause/target, offer targeted retry.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Repeated teaching covers missing cues or state.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Externalize recurring knowledge into the workflow.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Interface exposes backend terms or architecture as user workflow.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Rename/restructure around user goals and domain language.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Design/system problem is attributed to attention, intelligence, or resistance.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Investigate design evidence before blaming the person.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Feedback implies success while outcome is incomplete, failed, or ambiguous.
risk_registry.failure_consequence: missed failure or wrong next decision
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Separate accepted, processing, warning, partial success, success, and failure.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Compound operation hides item-level success/failure.
risk_registry.failure_consequence: failed subset ignored or all items rerun
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Show per-item status and targeted retry.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Workflow requires technical concepts beyond the user’s task role.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Use goal language, defaults, examples, and progressive disclosure.

risk_registry.primary_mechanism: Routine operation or recovery depends on one person’s memory.
risk_registry.preferred_prevention_or_recovery: Move expert knowledge into system cues, states, and recovery paths.

feedback_index.user_uncertainty_addressed: Did the system receive my action?
feedback_index.timing_requirement: within the perceptual moment after action
feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: Duplicate activation when acknowledgement is absent.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Button enters processing/accepted state tied to the target.

feedback_index.user_uncertainty_addressed: Is it still working or did it fail?
feedback_index.timing_requirement: periodic or milestone updates during delay
feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: High duplicate-action and abandonment risk during uncertainty.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Progress state names what is happening and what is safe to do.
feedback_index.bad_pattern: Indefinite spinner with no action target.

feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: May cause wrong next action rather than simple duplicate action.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Status message distinguishes accepted, processing, partial success, warning, and failure.
feedback_index.bad_pattern: Green toast saying Done without target/result.

feedback_index.timing_requirement: immediate and persistent enough to notice
feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: Very high repeat-action and abandonment risk.
Repeated checking or cancellation when progress is opaque.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Phase-level progress with current item and estimated next step when trustworthy.
feedback_index.bad_pattern: Spinner that hides phase and per-item status.

feedback_index.user_uncertainty_addressed: Is it finished and what should I do next?
feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: Duplicate work or missed output when completion is unclear.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Completion state names outputs and next action.
feedback_index.bad_pattern: Task ends by returning to idle with no result summary.

feedback_index.user_uncertainty_addressed: What failed, why, and what can I do?
feedback_index.timing_requirement: when failure is detected and close to source
feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: Recovery cost increases when error feedback lacks target and remedy.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Field/item-level error with targeted fix and preserved work.
feedback_index.bad_pattern: Generic red error with no source.

feedback_index.user_uncertainty_addressed: What succeeded, what failed, and what remains?
feedback_index.duplicate_action_risk: False success or redundant rework if partial outcome is collapsed.
feedback_index.good_pattern: Per-item status table with retry failed items.
feedback_index.bad_pattern: Single success/fail banner for a multi-item job.

mapping_index.correspondence_problem: User cannot predict which control changes which result.
mapping_index.user_prediction_required: Predict effect from control identity, position, and grouping.
mapping_index.good_mapping_pattern: Controls colocated with affected object and named by outcome.
mapping_index.bad_mapping_pattern: Controls separated from target or ordered by implementation.

mapping_index.correspondence_problem: Control structure does not correspond to user’s mental/spatial/task structure.
mapping_index.user_prediction_required: Use known spatial/task relation rather than memorized arbitrary mapping.
mapping_index.good_mapping_pattern: Arrange controls to mirror task sequence, object layout, or meaningful dimension.
mapping_index.bad_mapping_pattern: Alphabetical or database order when task order matters.

mapping_index.correspondence_problem: Proximity and layout do not show scope or target.
mapping_index.good_mapping_pattern: Put action inside or adjacent to its affected object/row.
mapping_index.bad_mapping_pattern: Global button next to local object with unclear scope.

mapping_index.correspondence_problem: Workflow order does not match the user’s task logic.
mapping_index.user_prediction_required: Predict next step from visible progress and task order.
mapping_index.good_mapping_pattern: Show step order, prerequisites, and current position.
mapping_index.bad_mapping_pattern: Free-form screen where hidden sequence matters.

mapping_index.correspondence_problem: Users cannot tell how filters change displayed metrics.
mapping_index.user_prediction_required: Predict which metrics and records change when filter changes.
mapping_index.good_mapping_pattern: Make filter scope persistent and tie each metric to active filters.
mapping_index.bad_mapping_pattern: Hidden global filter affects unrelated-looking cards.

constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: A warning leaves the user to track the relation mentally.

constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: A warning still allows invalid data to enter the workflow.

constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: A generic warning may be confirmed reflexively.

constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: A warning at submission forces rework after memory/context loss.

constraint_index.mechanism: keeps the user in a required state until safe completion
constraint_index.error_path_prevented: abandoning a process before critical completion
constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: warning may be ignored under time pressure
constraint_index.overconstraint_risk: can feel trapping if no safe cancel/recovery exists

constraint_index.mechanism: prevents action until safe state or permission exists
constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: warning still leaves unsafe action possible
constraint_index.overconstraint_risk: can hide available alternatives if reason is not communicated

constraint_index.what_warning_alone_would_fail_to_prevent: warning still depends on remembered sequence
constraint_index.overconstraint_risk: may slow expert workflows if condition is already obvious

conceptual_model_index.system_image_communicates: source files, terms, and control flow reveal an implementation-centered structure
conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when users ask why the workflow is arranged this way
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Align design around user task model and expose only necessary system logic.

conceptual_model_index.what_the_user_appears_to_believe: user may infer a simpler or different model
conceptual_model_index.system_image_communicates: interface names, state transitions, and feedback form the explanation
conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when user can operate but predicts wrong result
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Clarify the operating idea through labels, examples, state, and feedback.

conceptual_model_index.what_the_user_appears_to_believe: user believes actions affect different objects or states than they do
conceptual_model_index.system_image_communicates: observed predictions and explanations reveal beliefs
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Repair mismatch by changing system image or training only where design cannot carry the explanation.

conceptual_model_index.what_the_user_appears_to_believe: user infers operation from labels, layout, feedback, docs, and behavior
conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when interface and feedback contradict each other
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Make the perceivable system image coherent enough for prediction.

conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when users repeat action or choose wrong scope
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Expose state near the action it controls.

conceptual_model_index.what_the_user_appears_to_believe: user reasons in business goals rather than backend operations
conceptual_model_index.system_image_communicates: labels and workflow steps mirror implementation architecture
conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when users ask what technical terms mean
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Rename and restructure around user goals while keeping implementation detail in expert layers.

conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when users rely on trial and memory for exceptions
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Unify vocabulary, state meanings, and control behavior.

conceptual_model_index.system_image_communicates: labels require translation from expert to user terminology
conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when nontechnical users avoid capable tools
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Translate controls and status to target user language.

conceptual_model_index.where_mismatch_becomes_observable: when mistakes follow a plausible but wrong rule
conceptual_model_index.repair_direction: Make rule-selection cues visible and examples discriminating.

gulf_index.system_failure: The action mechanism or sequence is unclear.

gulf_index.system_failure: Labels or mappings do not connect user goal to control.
gulf_index.repair_direction: Rename, regroup, or remap actions around user goals.

gulf_index.system_failure: The required order is hidden or memory-dependent.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can a first-time user identify the next valid action without instructions?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add visible action signifiers or a state-aware primary action.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: A hidden next action creates an execution gulf before the user can even test the workflow.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which important action exists but has no perceivable cue at the point of need?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to expose the action through placement, label, handle, or alternate visible path.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: An unsupported cue strategy leaves the action available only to people who already know it.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does any visual cue suggest an action that the system does not actually support?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to remove false action styling or implement the implied action.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: False perceived affordances create wrong clicks and mistrust.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the label describe the user’s goal or the implementation?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to rename the action around user intent and remove implementation-model leakage.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Goal-language labels reduce translation work and wrong-rule plans.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can users explain the difference between neighboring actions before choosing?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to make labels, grouping, or consequences more discriminable.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Similar signifiers invite description-similarity slips.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the destructive action visually and semantically distinguishable from routine actions?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to separate, relabel, constrain, or make the action reversible.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: High-consequence actions need distinct commitment and recovery cues.

diagnostic_questions.question: What cue tells the user which object a control will affect?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to move or scope controls so action-target mapping is perceptually clear.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Poor scope signification produces wrong-object actions even when labels are readable.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is a critical action available only through a hidden gesture or shortcut?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add a visible redundant path or reveal the gesture.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Gesture-only access makes critical behavior dependent on expert memory.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can users predict which control changes a named result?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to reorganize controls around control-to-effect correspondence.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Mapping failures produce confident wrong actions, not just hesitation.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the workflow order match the user’s task order rather than database order?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to reorder steps or add a visible sequence.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Arbitrary order moves sequence knowledge into memory.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can users tell which row, file, or location a button applies to?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to change proximity, grouping, or selection-state display.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Scope ambiguity creates wrong-target actions in repeated item lists.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can users predict what a dashboard filter changes before applying it?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to show filter scope, affected metrics, and active-filter persistence.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Hidden filter mapping makes users interpret the wrong result set.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the action vocabulary organized by business goal rather than backend operation?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to replace implementation commands with goal-oriented controls.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Users should not need architecture knowledge to choose a routine action.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can users map each status indicator to the exact item it describes?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether compound operations need per-item status rather than one aggregate banner.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Item-level mapping prevents missed partial failures.

diagnostic_questions.question: What changes immediately after the user activates the control?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add action receipt and state transition feedback.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Immediate feedback prevents duplicate activation caused by uncertainty.

diagnostic_questions.question: What does the user know while a long-running process is still running?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add progress state, phase labels, and safe next-step guidance.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Delayed feedback widens the evaluation gulf and invites repeated action.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user distinguish accepted, processing, success, warning, partial success, and failure?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to split status states instead of using one generic success/failure message.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Collapsed states cause false success and wrong recovery decisions.

diagnostic_questions.question: What happens if one of several required uploads fails?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether the workflow needs a partial-success state, per-item status, and targeted retry.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Compound operations need feedback that preserves successful work while exposing failures.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the error message identify the failed item and repair action?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to move from generic error feedback to targeted recovery guidance.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Specific error feedback lowers recovery cost and expert dependence.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can users tell the difference between completion and idle state?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add completion summaries and next actions.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Returning silently to idle makes users rerun completed work or miss outputs.

diagnostic_questions.question: What invalid state does the system currently allow?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add constraints, prevalidation, or readiness gating.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Preventable invalid states should not be converted into late user errors.

diagnostic_questions.question: Would a warning still allow the harmful action to occur?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to replace warning-only design with a constraint or forcing function.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Warnings depend on memory and compliance when design could make error impossible.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which prerequisite is only revealed after the user fails?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to show prerequisite status before action and disable/gate until ready.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Late blockers waste effort and make users blame themselves.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the disabled action explain why it is unavailable and how to proceed?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether disabled controls need state-specific rationale and remedy.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Unexplained constraints create hidden-state confusion.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can logical relationships among required items be seen rather than remembered?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to expose one-to-one pairings, remaining items, or completeness checks.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Logical constraints only help when the relation is perceivable.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which cultural convention does this icon, color, or order assume?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to validate convention meaning with the target user population.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Cultural constraints can fail silently across groups.

diagnostic_questions.question: What does the user appear to believe the system will do?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to repair the system image or collect more evidence before redesign.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: A user’s prediction reveals conceptual-model mismatch better than a preference rating.

diagnostic_questions.question: What does the system image communicate through labels, state, feedback, and behavior?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to align the visible communication with the intended conceptual model.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Users learn the system from perceivable signals, not the designer’s internal model.

diagnostic_questions.question: Where does the user’s prediction first diverge from actual system behavior?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to change the cue at the mismatch point rather than rewriting the whole workflow.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: The mismatch point identifies the specific repair target.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which backend concept is being exposed as if it were the user’s task concept?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to hide, rename, or progressively disclose implementation detail.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Implementation-model leakage overloads nontechnical users and distorts action planning.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the same concept have different names or behaviors in different states?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to unify vocabulary and behavior across the system image.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Inconsistency makes users learn exceptions instead of a stable model.

diagnostic_questions.question: What rule did the user think applied, and what cue selected that rule?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to improve rule-discrimination cues or examples.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Rule-based mistakes are prevented by better rule conditions, not generic retraining.

diagnostic_questions.question: What must the user remember that is not visible?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Which procedural or state knowledge should be externalized into persistent UI cues.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: The question identifies fragile memory burdens before blaming forgetting.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which future action depends on the user remembering after a delay?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add reminders, pending state, or event-triggered prompts.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Prospective memory is fragile under delay and interruption.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which step order is currently carried in a cheat sheet or expert memory?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add a visible sequence, checklist, or interlock.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Sequence memory should not be required for routine nonexpert workflows.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which prerequisite is a user expected to know before opening this screen?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to surface readiness criteria and blockers in the workflow.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Hidden prerequisites convert missing system knowledge into user error.

diagnostic_questions.question: What file path, location, or folder rule must the user remember?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add recent items, breadcrumbs, selected-location state, or search.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Path memory creates wrong-location work when tasks are infrequent.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which naming convention could be shown as an example, default, or validator?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to replace arbitrary memorized naming with visible format support.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Naming rules are brittle when hidden and arbitrary.

diagnostic_questions.question: What mode or state is the user expected to remember across screens?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add persistent mode banners or reduce mode dependence.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Mode memory failures can turn correct intentions into wrong actions.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which rare recovery procedure only an expert knows?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to embed guided recovery or escalation in the error state.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Rare recovery cannot depend on practiced memory.

diagnostic_questions.question: What knowledge is distributed across people or devices without a shared state?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add ownership, timestamps, or shared status.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Distributed hidden knowledge creates duplicate work and missed handoffs.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user resume after interruption without remembering where they were?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add persistent state, checkpoints, and a resume summary.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Real workflows include interruption; design must support resumption.

diagnostic_questions.question: What user goal is active at the failure point?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to map available actions to the actual goal rather than the screen structure.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: A goal-action mismatch identifies an execution-gulf repair.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which action appears available, and which action actually achieves the goal?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to change signifiers, labels, grouping, or action availability.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Execution fails when apparent action and effective action diverge.

diagnostic_questions.question: What sequence does the user think is required?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to externalize workflow order or correct a mistaken sequence model.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Sequence expectations reveal whether the problem is execution or understanding.

diagnostic_questions.question: What invalid or dangerous action is possible at this step?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to constrain, disable, or redesign the action path.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Allowed invalid actions convert preventable design issues into user errors.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the same action mean different things in different modes?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to reduce mode dependence or make mode state persistent.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Mode-dependent actions are a specific execution risk, not generic confusion.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user state what happened after the action?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether feedback content needs to report result, target, and state.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Evaluation depends on interpretable post-action evidence.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user tell whether the system is working during delay?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add progress or heartbeat feedback.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: People repeat or abandon action when processing state is unknowable.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user distinguish successful completion from partial success?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add item-level and aggregate outcome states.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Partial failure hidden behind success creates downstream errors.

diagnostic_questions.question: What system state is hidden at the moment of decision?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to show selection, filter, mode, or readiness near the dependent action.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Hidden state makes correct evaluation impossible.

diagnostic_questions.question: What decision is this result supposed to help the user make?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add thresholds, definitions, explanations, or next actions.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Dashboard and report outputs must support interpretation, not just display data.

diagnostic_questions.question: What should the user do next after this result?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether terminal states need next-action, retry, exit, or escalation paths.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: A result without next-step meaning leaves the workflow unfinished.

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the user form the correct goal but execute the wrong action?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to treat the event as a slip and focus on execution supports.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Slip prevention differs from mistake prevention.

diagnostic_questions.question: Did a frequent routine capture a less frequent intended sequence?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add a goal checkpoint or differentiate the uncommon path at divergence.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Capture slips are driven by habit dominance after a shared start.

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the wrong target share name, position, or appearance with the intended target?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to increase target discrimination.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Description-similarity slips require distinguishing targets, not general warnings.

diagnostic_questions.question: Was a planned step forgotten after interruption or delay?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add resumption cues, reminders, or visible sequence state.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Memory-lapse errors can occur despite correct understanding.

diagnostic_questions.question: What did the user believe the current mode was?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to make mode visible, separate mode-specific controls, or remove mode dependence.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Mode errors turn correct intentions into wrong outcomes.

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the user choose the wrong goal, rule, or plan?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to treat the event as a mistake and repair model/rule cues.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Mistakes need conceptual or rule support rather than only execution safeguards.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which rule did the user apply, and why did it seem appropriate?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to clarify rule-selection cues and exceptions.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Rule-based mistakes are often rational under misleading cues.

diagnostic_questions.question: Was the situation novel enough that the user lacked an adequate model?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add conceptual explanation, examples, or safe preview.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Knowledge-based mistakes emerge where no reliable rule is available.

diagnostic_questions.question: Did social or time pressure make a violation seem rational?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to redesign incentives, workload, or reporting rather than blame the operator.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Violations may be symptoms of system pressure.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can this error be made impossible rather than merely warned about?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to use a constraint or forcing function instead of warning copy.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Preventing impossible states is stronger than relying on attention.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the confirmation asking for a meaningful decision or creating habituation?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to replace generic confirmation with target-specific commitment or undo.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Low-value confirmations become another rote action.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the system preserve user work after this error?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to store drafts, keep field values, or retain successful items.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Recovery cost drives abandonment and expert dependence.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is retry targeted to the failed item or does it repeat successful work?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add per-item retry and idempotency safeguards.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Untargeted retry creates duplicate work and hides the original failure.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user recover without expert help?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add guided repair, visible error state, or clear escalation.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Expert-only recovery makes routine operations fragile.

diagnostic_questions.question: What evidence should be preserved for human review?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether escalation should capture inputs, state, logs, and user intent.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Escalation without context shifts diagnostic burden to people.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which fields are truly necessary for the user’s goal and system decision?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to remove, defer, or justify fields.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Unnecessary fields increase abandonment and data-entry error paths.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user distinguish required, optional, and conditionally required fields?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to change labels, grouping, or branching.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Requirement ambiguity causes late validation errors and hesitation.

diagnostic_questions.question: When can the system know the field is invalid?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether validation should happen inline, on blur, after dependency, or on submit.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Validation timing should match knowability and avoid premature interruption.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the error message perceptually close to the field or action that caused it?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to move error placement and preserve context.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Distance between error and source adds mapping and memory burden.

diagnostic_questions.question: What happens if the user clicks submit twice?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add immediate submission state, duplicate prevention, and idempotency boundary.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Duplicate submission is often feedback/state uncertainty, not impatience.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does branching hide why a later question appears?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to show branch logic or progressive context.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Hidden branching can create conceptual-model confusion in forms.

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the user tell the active scope, time range, and filters of every metric?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to persist scope near metrics and exports.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Metrics without scope invite false interpretation.

diagnostic_questions.question: What action should a dashboard user take from this status?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add decision thresholds, status explanations, and next actions.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Information display is not decision support unless interpretation is possible.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which expert explanation could the tool communicate itself?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to embed examples, state, recovery, or labels that replace repeated expert help.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Expert dependency is often a knowledge-in-world design gap.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which step depends on knowing folder architecture, metric IDs, or backend terms?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to hide implementation structure behind user-goal workflows.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Operational tools should not require backend architecture understanding from nontechnical users.

diagnostic_questions.question: What actual user evidence supports this diagnosis?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to label the output as a tested finding, a hypothesis, or a principle-based risk.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: AI agents must not turn plausible mechanism matching into certainty.

diagnostic_questions.question: What competing HCD diagnosis could also explain the same behavior?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to collect more observation before recommending a specific redesign.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Many behaviors, such as hesitation, have multiple possible causes.

diagnostic_questions.question: Which source-supported claim is being used, and which claim is an applied extension?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to move applied pattern statements out of directly_supported_claims.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Source traceability fails when modern software recommendations are presented as direct book claims.

diagnostic_questions.question: Are current accessibility, browser, platform, or framework claims being assumed?
diagnostic_questions.decision_it_informs: Whether to add a verification flag and consult current authoritative documentation.
diagnostic_questions.why_it_matters: Stable HCD principles do not substitute for current technical/accessibility verification.

current_verification_flags.why_time_sensitive: WCAG/accessibility requirements change and require current authoritative verification.
Browser behavior, file inputs, and form submission handling can change.
Mobile OS, camera, and browser handling vary over time.
Screen readers and assistive technologies depend on current platform semantics.
Current platform conventions shape signifiers and cultural constraints.
GAS APIs, quotas, and UI options change over time.
Streamlit controls, state, and forms evolve.
Form platforms change validation, localization, and branching capabilities.
Custom components need current implementation and AT verification.
Auth, audit, and permission requirements are time-sensitive.
Logs, reports, and user behavior data require current privacy review.
Language, locale, input, and translation guidance evolve.
